headline: Linking GWAS loci in crops to prioritized non-coding and structural variants
label: Variant Prioritization And Association Mapping
summary: Population resequencing and chromatin-aware sequence models now move association signals toward candidate variants in plant and mammalian genomes.
synthesis: The common thread is the reduction of association output to candidate variants. The rice preprint fine-tunes a DNA language model on ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq chromatin data to prioritize non-coding variants within GWAS loci. The soybean study resequences 940 accessions plus public data, yielding 602,281 SVs and graph-based presence-absence variants, with GWAS linking these structural variants to agronomic traits. The 3'UTR study identifies highly conserved fragments across mammals and characterizes them with a transformer model. The items differ in data type and aim: computational non-coding prioritization in crops, population structural variant discovery, and conserved regulatory element analysis in mammals. What is new is the combination of population-scale variant catalogs with chromatin-level annotation and sequence-model scoring, which assigns putative function to specific variants within association loci.
